# Quizkit JSON format

[Türkçe](format.tr.md)

Quizkit imports two shapes of JSON: a **single quiz**, or a **collection** of quizzes in folders. The app tells them apart by itself: an object with `"questions"` is a single quiz; one with `"folders"` or `"quizzes"` is a collection. Files can be up to 10 MB.

## Single quiz

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `schemaVersion` | yes | Always `1`. |
| `title` | yes | 1–120 characters. |
| `description` | no | Any text. |
| `language` | no | For example `"tr"` or `"en"`. |
| `questions` | yes | 1–5000 questions. |

Each question:

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `question` | yes | The question text. |
| `options` | yes | 2–6 texts. Do not prefix them with `A)`. |
| `answer` | yes | Letter of the correct option: `"A"` for the first, `"B"` for the second… (A–F, any case). |
| `explanation` | no | Why the answer is right. Shown after answering in Practice mode and in the review. |
| `tags` | no | A list of texts. |
| `id` | no | Must be unique within the quiz. |

Example ([examples/quiz.en.json](../examples/quiz.en.json)):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "title": "Biology – Cell Structure",
  "language": "en",
  "questions": [
    {
      "question": "Which organelle produces most of the cell's ATP?",
      "options": [
        "Nucleus",
        "Ribosome",
        "Mitochondrion",
        "Golgi apparatus",
        "Lysosome"
      ],
      "answer": "C",
      "explanation": "Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, which produces most of the ATP."
    }
  ]
}
```

## Collection (quizzes in folders)

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `schemaVersion` | yes | Always `1`, once at the top. |
| `folders` | no | Folders, each `{ "name", "quizzes", "folders" }`. |
| `quizzes` | no | Quizzes at the top level (same as a single quiz, `schemaVersion` not needed). |

- A folder can contain quizzes and subfolders; folders can be nested up to 8 levels.
- A file can contain up to 500 quizzes.
- On import you choose a target folder. Folders with the same name (ignoring upper/lower case) are reused instead of duplicated.
- Quizzes already in the library are skipped. A quiz with errors is skipped and its errors are listed; the others are still imported.

Example ([examples/collection.en.json](../examples/collection.en.json)):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "folders": [
    {
      "name": "Economics",
      "folders": [
        {
          "name": "2023",
          "quizzes": [
            {
              "title": "Economics – Midterm 2023",
              "questions": [
                {
                  "question": "According to the law of demand, what happens to quantity demanded when the price rises?",
                  "options": [
                    "It rises",
                    "It falls",
                    "It stays the same",
                    "It rises, then falls",
                    "It becomes zero"
                  ],
                  "answer": "B",
                  "explanation": "All else equal, price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions."
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "quizzes": [
        {
          "title": "Economics – Unit 1",
          "questions": [
            {
              "question": "Which science studies how scarce resources are allocated to unlimited wants?",
              "options": [
                "Sociology",
                "Economics",
                "Law",
                "Psychology",
                "Geography"
              ],
              "answer": "B"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Writing texts

- Plain text only: no Markdown, HTML or images. A line break is `\n`.
- Quotation marks inside a text: use `“ ”` or `\"`. A plain `"` ends the JSON string.
- Math: LaTeX inside `$...$` (inline) or `$$...$$` (own line). Inside JSON, double every backslash: `\\frac{1}{2}`. A `$` followed by a digit counts as a price, not math; `\\$` is a literal dollar sign.
- Images are not supported yet; an `image` field is ignored with a warning.

## What the app repairs by itself

These common AI mistakes are fixed on import, with a warning so you know:

- Text or code fences around the JSON.
- Curly quotes used as JSON quotes.
- LaTeX written with single backslashes (`\frac` instead of `\\frac`).
- Plain quotation marks inside a text.

Anything else is reported with the question number, the line and column, and the faulty line.
